Research experience

DynaInterfere-Bench: Robotic Manipulation under Dynamic Interference

2026–Present

Research collaboration with Dr. Kaichen Zhou (Massachusetts Institute of Technology) and Prof. Fangneng Zhan (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)

Controlled benchmarking of vision-language-action (VLA) policies, baseline evaluation, and training-free recovery under dynamic interference.

  • Co-developed an Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab benchmark with six YAM Ultra2 manipulation tasks, randomized layouts, collision-aware expert planning, and configurable visual occlusion and periodic or reactive obstacles.
  • Contributed to 2,000 successful demonstrations (800 xArm5; 1,200 Ultra2), including dual-camera capture, image–state–action synchronization checks, separate train/test seeds, and LeRobot exports.
  • Integrated π0.5 and X-VLA action adapters; contributed to four-epoch, full-parameter X-VLA fine-tuning on four RTX 5090 GPUs, including checkpoint validation and recovery.
  • Evaluated fine-tuned π0.5 and X-VLA in 400 seed-matched xArm5 trials per model. Baseline success was 83.75% and 99.75%, respectively, under a shared 90-second task-and-return-home protocol.
  • Integrated Astra and Sol into an RGB-based robot control pipeline with structured Cartesian and gripper commands, inverse kinematics, and execution feedback. Validated bounded motion with Astra and exploratory mug pick-and-place with Sol without task-specific fine-tuning.
  • Prototyped a model-agnostic, training-free runtime adapter for risk monitoring, braking, avoidance, and trajectory rejoining, with an initial 12-pair on/off study (24 rollouts). Exploring temporal memory and multi-view 3D context for robustness to occlusion.

Halo Copilot / SmartHat

Feb 2026–Present

Graduate Researcher · Creative Machines Lab, Columbia University · Advised by Prof. Hod Lipson

A wearable assembly assistant combining RGB-D perception, spatially aligned projection, and multimodal step assessment.

  • Developed a wearable camera–projector system on Jetson Orin Nano with Intel RealSense D435i sensing to provide guidance on physical workspaces.
  • Combined 13-class YOLO part detection with Lucas–Kanade optical flow and adaptive detection scheduling for continuous localization during assembly.
  • Implemented depth-plane estimation, calibrated camera-to-projector mapping, and confidence-aware rendering to keep projected guidance aligned as viewpoints change.
  • Integrated GPT-6.1-sol for multimodal step-completion assessment against an eight-step XML-defined assembly plan; investigating diagnosis of missing or incorrectly installed parts.

Training-Free Asynchronous Control for World-Action Models

World Assembly

Execution-aware inference and asynchronous control for pretrained FastWAM policies.

  • Developed training-free asynchronous control extensions combining continuous policy inference, execution-progress-aware action alignment, and hold-aware action stitching.
  • Implemented multiprocess simulation and inference backends with dedicated GPU allocation, Pipe-based interprocess communication, reduced observation payloads, and per-stage latency profiling.
  • Conducted RoboTwin baseline and ablation evaluations across 12 manipulation tasks, with 30 rollouts per method (720 total evaluation rollouts).

Selected robotics projects

8-DOF Quadruped Robot

Columbia University · Robotics Studio

  • Designed and built an 8-DOF quadruped using LX-16A smart servos and Raspberry Pi 4B, integrating mechanical design, inverse kinematics, gait generation, embedded actuation, and physical-robot testing.
  • Developed a MuJoCo simulation and trained locomotion policies with PPO; compared learned control with manually designed gaits and investigated practical sim-to-real transfer issues.
